key_insight: BEAKER reveals a gap between MLLMs’ coarse understanding of laboratory procedures and the precise, action-grounded perception needed to execute them.
engineering_relevance: Autonomous chemistry systems need targeted validation of operable regions, feasible trajectories, apparatus states, and safety constraints before relying on MLLMs for execution.
method: Benchmark embodied laboratory capabilities across 11 image and video task types.
Use questions and annotations manually created and reviewed by chemistry and embodied AI experts, without AI assistance.
Evaluate 28 general-purpose, science-oriented, chemistry-specialized, and embodied MLLMs.
evidence_signal: Across 1,000 expert-curated question-answer samples, offline single-turn evaluation finds stronger coarse video-procedure understanding but persistent difficulties with action grounding, fine-grained recognition, and mid-length step ordering.
watch_item: Offline, single-turn benchmark performance does not establish safe or reliable closed-loop execution in physical laboratories.
paper_title: BEAKER: An Expert-Curated Benchmark for Embodied Brains in Self-Driving Chemical Laboratories
